subject: Onboarding & order form: PO acknowledgement SLA and transfer method
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@helixlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood onboarding: data residency + PO transfer method (Ariba vs API)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — Helix is keen to proceed with Redwood but procurement has two gating items before we can complete Ariba registration and push the PO flow live:

1) PO acknowledgement SLA: we need 24-hour PO ACK for all EMEA orders or an SLA amendment in the order form.
2) Transfer method: procurement prefers an API/webhook-based PO push to our ERP, rather than nightly SFTP. Can Redwood support both (API push + SFTP fallback)?

Also, legal flagged a data-residency line for EU customer data in the order form — they want confirmation of EU-hosted inference for Helix workloads. I’ve attached the draft order form our team started (see Helix_OrderForm_Draft.pdf).

Can you confirm next steps and internal contacts for legal and solutions to work the redline? We’ll need a DocuSign-ready order form and a short mutual action plan to get Ariba registration queued.

Best,
Elena
Head of Procurement
Helix Labs
[Attachment: Helix_OrderForm_Draft.pdf (pdf)]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@helixlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 12:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding: data residency + PO transfer method (Ariba vs API)

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary and for attaching the draft. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Karthik (Solutions) who will help with the order form and integration options.

Quick answers:
- We can support a push-style API + webhook for PO delivery (preferred) and keep SFTP as an operational fallback.
- For EU-hosting we have a Private deployment option (customer-controlled VPC) or can pin hosted workloads to our eu-central-1 region; Marissa will confirm the exact contractual language to state that.
- We can include a 24-hour PO acknowledgement SLA as an addendum to the order form, plus a fallback SLA where webhook retries are attempted for X hours before SFTP is used.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Marissa to propose redline language for the MSA/order form covering PO ACK SLA and data residency.
2) Karthik to draft the integration runbook (API endpoints, headers, sample payload, webhook retry policy) for Helix to review — that will feed Ariba vs API decisions.
3) I’ll prepare a mutual action plan and a DocuSign-ready order form once redlines are agreed.

Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0129
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@helixlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding: data residency + PO transfer method (Ariba vs API)

Thanks for the context. I reviewed Helix's draft and put together a short set of proposed contract edits (see attached "Helix_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf"). High-level comments below — these are intended to be narrow, procurement-friendly edits so we can keep the order form straightforward while covering the key asks.

Key redline proposals:
- PO Acknowledgement SLA: Add Section 2.3(a) to the order form: "Provider will acknowledge receipt of a valid Purchase Order within twenty-four (24) hours of receipt. Acknowledgement may be via API webhook or secure SFTP confirmation; when both are configured, Provider will attempt webhook delivery and will fall back to SFTP after two (2) retry cycles."

- Data residency: Add order-form option checkbox and language: "Customer may elect EU residency for inference workloads. Where EU residency is elected, Provider will operate inference workloads in eu-central-1 (or customer-provided, mutually-agreed VPC in EU) for the duration of the Order Form. Provider will not transfer EEA customer content outside the EEA without Customer instruction."

- Liability/Indemnity: We will not accept unlimited liability. Propose cap equal to annual fees under the order form, with carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct.

- Evidence: Attach SOC 2 Type II summary + pointer to compliance package; we can provide audit artifacts under NDA if Helix needs deeper proof.

Operational notes for Karthik: please prepare the API endpoint description and a sample webhook schema. Helix asked about EDI invoice windows — we should propose a 7-calendar-day window for invoice reconciliation if using EDI, with 48-hour invoice ACK for API receipts.

I’ve kept the redlines minimal so this can move to DocuSign quickly; attaching the redline PDF for review.

Marissa Cole
Head of Contracts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Helix_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf (pdf)]
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@helixlabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Dec 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding: data residency + PO transfer method (Ariba vs API)

Marissa / Soojin — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick items from procurement/legal after internal review: 

- The 24-hour PO ACK via webhook + 2 retry cycles is acceptable. We want the retry policy documented in the integration runbook (retries, exponential backoff, idempotency token).
- For invoice windows: Helix prefers a 10-calendar-day reconciliation window for EDI invoices (we're willing to accept 7 if Redwood can provide automated invoice match logs).
- Data residency checkbox is fine; we will elect EU residency in the order form. The SOC 2 pointer is good — procurement will sign an NDA for audit artifacts if needed.

Can you send a DocuSign-ready order form with the redlined language and a 1-page MOP (method of proceeding) that lists the integration steps, required test POs, and runbook links? If you can get that to us early next week we’ll start our Ariba registration in parallel and schedule a 30-min runbook review with our ERP team.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Elena
